takeaway: Expiratory reserve volume is the maximum volume that can be expired after a normal tidal expiration, so it excludes tidal volume. Residual volume stays in the lungs.

question.text: When analysing a spirogram, the expiratory reserve volume is defined as which one of the following?

answer.text: The maximum volume expired during forced breathing excluding the tidal volume

lines.text: A spirogram traces each breath on moving paper.
The small waves are tidal volume, the air in a normal breath.
After a normal breath out, you can force out much more air.
That extra volume is the expiratory reserve volume.
It does not include the tidal volume, we cut that part away.
Some air always stays behind in the lungs, and that is the residual volume.
So expiratory reserve is forced expiration, excluding tidal volume.
